strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis: Clear categorization of attention patterns and important observation that low-entropy tokens suffer disproportionately from cache eviction (147% vs 52% loss increase), providing genuine insights into KV cache behavior

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive testing across multiple models and benchmarks with thorough ablations, generalization studies on out-of-domain datasets, and significant demonstrated speedups (up to 9.79×)
Principled two-stage training approach: Golden Eviction provides theoretically justified supervision; RL refinement addresses distribution shift; efficient MLP scorer (2.7% overhead)

Strong empirical results: Achieves comparable performance with half the KV cache budget; preserves 92-99% of original performance under strict constraints; consistent improvements across multiple models
Solid experimental methodology: Multiple baselines including recent methods, robust budget generalization, good presentation with clear figures and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Scoring models are established (H2O, SnapKV), GRPO borrowed from DeepSeek, Golden Eviction is straightforward use of future max attention, and low-entropy targeting is incremental—contribution is primarily in engineering combination rather than novel methodology

Critical training-inference gap: Golden Eviction requires full-sequence future attention (Eq. 5) only available during training; inference must approximate without this oracle information; sufficiency of learned approximation not rigorously analyzed, and performance degradation from this gap is not quantified

Weak theoretical analysis: Appendix A bound (2Cϵt) is intuitive and loose; doesn't account for model adaptation or error compounding over long sequences; no analysis of whether learned scorer maintains theoretical guarantees during inference

Ad-hoc reward function design: Focus on low-entropy tokens (bottom 80%, loss threshold η=1.5) appears empirically tuned without principled justification; choice of MSE loss vs. alternatives (Eq. 8) seems arbitrary

Training data constraints: Requires filtered subset of corrected long traces; unclear sensitivity to training data quality/diversity; all training on math reasoning limits understanding of broader applicability; MiniCPM shows architectural sensitivity not explained

strengths: Compelling empirical analysis in Section 2 identifying distinct attention patterns (global, position-dependent, semantic-dependent) and demonstrating disproportionate loss increases for low-entropy tokens (+75% to +187%), providing clear motivation for the approach

Principled two-stage training framework combining supervised learning via Golden Eviction (grounded in theoretical analysis in Appendix A) with RL refinement, showing how to leverage future information for eviction decisions

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Qwen3-4B/1.7B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, MiniCPM, Qwen3-14B/32B) and benchmarks (AIME2024/2025, GPQA, LiveCodeBench, LongBench) with extensive ablations and generalization studies
Strong and practical results achieving comparable performance to baselines with only half the KV cache budget and substantial throughput improvements (up to 9.79× on 32K generation)
Practical design with lightweight scoring models requiring no LLM parameter updates and minimal computational overhead (2.7% of total time), enabling easy integration into existing systems
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (reward formulations, model architecture, sampling strategies) and sensitivity analyses for hyperparameters
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: the approach primarily combines existing techniques (MLP scoring, pairwise ranking loss, GRPO) with future attention scores and low-entropy focus, rather than introducing fundamentally new ideas or insights

Significant theoretical gaps: Proposition A.1 assumes bounded value vectors and local Lipschitz properties without empirical validation; no verification that these conditions hold in deep networks; the connection from minimizing evicted attention mass to generation quality is indirect

Golden Eviction algorithm limitations inadequately discussed: uses max pooling (potentially overly conservative), block size L has no sensitivity analysis, and requires expensive training data (full sequences with ground-truth outputs and future attention)

RL stage appears underutilized: improvements over supervised-only training are often modest (typically 2-3 points on benchmarks in Table 3), with insufficient justification for why RL is necessary when supervised training achieves most gains

Evaluation narrowly focused on math reasoning tasks: primary benchmarks are AIME2024/2025; generalization experiments (GPQA, LiveCodeBench) are limited; no evaluation on truly different long-generation domains (creative writing, dialogue, multi-turn conversations); training on STILL dataset may bias policy

Training requirements limit practical applicability: requires generating full sequences with ground-truth correct outputs, which is expensive and may bias learning; only trained on 'corrected traces'; generalization to new LLMs/domains unclear with evidence of model-specific hyperparameter tuning (different β values)

Insufficient hyperparameter sensitivity analysis: many critical hyperparameters (block size L, budget B, entropy threshold, loss threshold η, margin m) but limited exploration; block size L not varied despite being fundamental to Golden Eviction

Missing technical justification: Golden Eviction uses max pooling without explanation of why max over average; reward uses MSE (Eq. 8) without principled derivation; design choice of Top-K multinomial sampling justified empirically (Table 5) but not theoretically

Limited comparison with related training-based methods: G-KV, DuoAttention, RPC comparisons relegated to Table 17; no comparison with supervised-only approach as main baseline; most recent methods (Lancucki et al., 2025) not compared in primary results

Reproducibility concerns: code not available for review; no random seed reporting despite stochastic sampling; attention features details in appendix; training data filtering ('corrected traces') not fully specified
